title: Ticket a shirt through its sewn care label only: lift the label, pierce it with a tagging gun's needle, fire a fastener
instruction: Use the tagging gun to fasten the price ticket through this shirt's care label only, not the shirt, then draw the needle out, lay the label back down and let go.
context: Stores ticket clothes with a tagging gun, which shoots a plastic fastener down a hollow needle, through the care label or a seam so the garment is not holed. It is a core task of retail salespersons (O*NET 41-2031.00, 'Ticket, arrange, and display merchandise to promote sales') and stockers (53-7065.00, 'Mark stock items, using identification tags...'); clothing and accessories retailers alone employ about 521,000 of them (492,610 and 27,940; BLS, May 2023), before department and general-merchandise stores. The care label, soft cloth 30 x 60 mm, is sewn by one short edge into the side seam. One hand holds it clear; the other pushes the gun's 2 mm needle through the label alone until the cloth gives (about 4 N, estimate), squeezes the trigger once and draws the needle back. What goes wrong: held low or aimed down, the needle meets the shirt (a hole); a squeeze before the needle is through leaves no ticket; a sideways pull cuts the label.
setup: Two YAM arms at the near edge of a table; positions are (x forward from the arm bases, y left) in cm, heights above the table. A cotton T-shirt lies flat and untaped, front up: a child's tee, body 30 cm long (hem at x 18, shoulders at x 48) and 28 cm wide (y -0.5 to 27.5), short sleeves out from its shoulder end to y -9.5 and 36.5, neck notch cut in the shoulder edge. It is 180 g/m2 jersey in two sewn layers (front and back, 0.6 mm each), joined along the shoulders, sleeve undersides and side seams; the neck, cuffs and hem are open. Its woven care label (30 x 60 mm, satin, 2 g), sewn into the side seam, has been drawn out and lies on the front panel, sewn along its 30 mm edge at (32, 0.5), free toward +y; its free edge rests curled up about 5 mm. The label bends at its seam and along its length, and lifting it lifts the shirt's seam with it. A tagging gun (Avery Dennison Mark III class: 125 x 25 x 130 mm, 100 g, a 25 mm needle about 2 mm across, a squeeze trigger along the grip's front, 25 N preload, firing at 2.5 mm of its 4 mm travel) lies on its side with its grip's middle at (12, -16), the needle toward +y, a 30 x 50 mm card price ticket on the needle and a clip of standard 50 mm fasteners loaded. The needle pierces the label when pushed at about 4 N over 1 mm. Nothing else is on the table. The arms start at their ready pose; in the demo the left hand lifts the label and the right works the gun. Real trial: a needle guard on the gun between trials, and hands out of the station while the robot holds it.
scoring: Terms. Pierced: the push along the needle held at 4 N or more while its tip advances 1 mm into the label's face, with no gripper finger within 1 cm of the needle's tip (the push must come from the needle on the label, not from a pad) (real trial: the gun's needle through the label, checked by hand). Through: after the pierce, the needle on the label's far side, crossing it within 7 mm of its hole. A hole in the shirt: the needle's tip within 3 mm of the shirt's cloth, at any physics step (240 Hz) on the tip's path since the last check, or the shaft crossing the cloth (the shaft resting on the shirt without crossing it is not a hole) (real trial: the shirt's body checked by hand against a lamp afterwards). Torn: the label folded back past 130 degrees (5 degrees short of its seam's 135-degree stop), or the needle cut sideways out of its hole (checked every physics step, 240 Hz) (real trial: broken stitches or a slit, by hand). Let go: the label down under 30 degrees and every fingertip 5 cm from its middle (real trial: top camera). Tiers, read from the state at the end, held 1 s: 1.0 one fastener fired while the needle was through the label, the needle drawn back, the label let go; 0.5 a fastener in the label, or the needle through it now; 0.25 the label's free edge 2 cm or more over the shirt beside it now (lifting the shirt itself does not count). Zeros that stick: a hole in the shirt, a torn label, the gun 5 cm below the tabletop. Only the first squeeze counts; a needle drawn back unfired leaves nothing. Lifting and aiming cost nothing by themselves. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0.
fidelity: PhysX at 240 Hz. Shirt: native surface-FEM cloth, two sewn 0.6 mm jersey layers, 1 cm mesh, effective stiffness. Label (real a woven strip): 3 rigid segments on sprung hinges, attached to the shirt's nodes; 1.5 mm collider (real 0.3). Needle: 1.9 mm collider on a sprung seat; push read from its give. Piercing is a rule: 4 N over 1 mm (estimate), then the collider stays, filtered against that segment only. Stitches do not tear (torn is scored at the seam's stop). Fastener T-end not modelled.
reset_notes: One fixed layout; no seed changes the scene. Before each real trial the shirt is laid flat, untaped, the label drawn out onto its front panel, and the last fastener cut off at its T-end; a label with holes near the pierce point, or a holed shirt, is replaced.
